subject: Cross-border standby SLA carveout — limited RTO/RPO for jurisdictional constraints
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon.park@greenlakebank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@greenlakebank.com
Date: Tue, 1 Oct 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: regional RTO/RPO carveout for cross-border failover

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. As we move into procurement, we ran the proposed multi-region failover against our legal/compliance guidance and hit a blocker: several of our EU-hosted customer datasets are regulated to remain within EU borders during normal operations and for primary backups. That restricts automatic failover to our US warm standby without additional approvals.

Concretely, GreenLake is asking whether Redwood can support a limited SLA carveout for cross-border failover where:
- Failover to non-EU region is permitted only after a manual approval window with documented steps.
- RTO for cross-border activation may be extended to up to 6 hours (rather than your typical 30/60 min).
- RPO could be relaxed to a max of 4 hours for cross-border cases.

We recognize this is a deviation from standard multi-region SLOs. Our security team attached the questionnaire; procurement will need a written amendment that calls out the carveout and an associated runbook, mitigation controls (encryption, KMS region binding), and an agreed escalation path.

Attachment: GreenLake_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Can you confirm if Redwood would consider a carveout like this and what mitigations you would require?

Best,
Simon Park
Head of Cloud Ops
GreenLake Bank
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon.park@greenlakebank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Oct 2029 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regional RTO/RPO carveout for cross-border failover

Simon —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sending the questionnaire. We can absolutely work with constraints like this, but it will require a documented exception (amendment) to the standard SLA and a set of compensating controls. High level, we typically propose a phased approach:

1) Technical mitigations: KMS key-per-region, at-rest and in-transit encryption, and a pre-authorized but manual playbook for cross-border activation.
2) Operational mitigations: a canary activation window to validate the runbook, explicit runbook sign-off from your security team, and a quarterly joint DR test for cross-border scenarios.
3) Commercial mitigations: a limited carveout clause with agreed credits if we miss the extended RTO/RPO bounds during cross-border activations.

Can you share the security team's must-have list from the questionnaire? Karthik and Naomi — looping you in to draft the operational appendix and to size the canary run.

I'll schedule a 30-min call for Thurs to go through the questionnaire responses and map action owners.

— Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon.park@greenlakebank.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Oct 2029 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regional RTO/RPO carveout for cross-border failover

Simon — thanks for the questionnaire. I reviewed the items relevant to failover and drafted a pragmatic proposal attached. TL;DR of our proposal:

- Cross-border activation will be manual and require a documented request from GreenLake Ops + an executive approval from your security lead.
- We propose an agreed activation SLA for cross-border scenarios: RTO = 6 hours (from approval), RPO = 4 hours.
- During the manual activation window Redwood will enable a restricted failover path that preserves audit logs, enforces KMS key usage in originating region where possible, and keeps traffic routing within approved endpoints.
- We will include a rollback policy and a mandatory post-activation post-mortem within 72 hours.

Commercially, we propose the following guardrails: the carveout is limited to the GreenLake account and requires a 12-month operational attachment. If Redwood fails to meet the extended RTO/RPO during a cross-border activation, we will issue credits up to 10% of monthly committed fees for the month of the event.

See attached: regional-fallback-proposal.xlsx for the SOP, timeline for a canary test, and required signoff checklist.

If this looks reasonable, Markus, can Legal spin an amendment and Procurement/Sales take care of signature mechanics?

— Naomi Feldman
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Simon Park <simon.park@greenlakebank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@greenlakebank.com
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 07:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regional RTO/RPO carveout for cross-border failover

Naomi, Markus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the pragmatic proposal. A few procurement/controls follow-ups before Legal starts redlining:
- We need the explicit escalation path: contact names, phone numbers, and on-call rotation for cross-border activations.
- Procurement requires a statement confirming that the carveout applies only to data classes X,Y,Z and the rest of the workload remains subject to standard multi-region SLA.
- Please include an explicit DocuSign link to the amendment so we can track signatures.

I'll also attach our procurement checklist for reference. If you can provide the above items and the canary window dates (we prefer late Oct), we can get the procurement queue moving.

Attachment: procurement_requirements.docx

Best,
Simon Park
Head of Cloud Ops
GreenLake Bank
